page.overview:
Who is Jianjun?

Jianjun was a Fire National, but spent a substantial part of her youth in the Earth Kingdom. As a result, she had an innate understanding of many Earth Kingdom traditions. After reaching adulthood, she enlisted in the Fire Army and was accepted into the personal guard of General Uyanga, As a result of her duties, she spent much time with her superior's family and became the protector of Uyanga's young son. Seeing him grow up and growing close to him, Jianjun began to regard the boy as a surrogate son.

Her life greatly changed when Haoran's insurgents attacked Uyanga's estate, partially collapsing it. Jianjun was at the side of Uyanga's son at the time of the attack, and the two were trapped under rubble together. Whereas the soldier was left emotionally scarred, the boy was heavily injured. When Uyanga subsequently declared her intention to hunt and destroy Haoran's rebels at all costs, Jianjun volunteered to aid this mission to avenge her ward's suffering.

As a result of her skills at manipulation, Jianjun was sent out as a spy to find the insurgents. She soon managed to discover that the militants had linked up with a group of refugees at Maizu Village. There, Jianjun spread the rumor that a Fire Nation attack was imminent, causing a panic as the civilians ran for safety. Amid this chaos, the spy joined the refugees' ranks and began traveling with them as well as Haoran's rebels. Leaving coded messages behind, she allowed Uyanga's troops to trail them. The general chased the mixed Earth Kingdom group over the next month. Though she gradually realized that endangering the refugees during this hunt was morally questionable, Jianjun continued to do her duty until the refugees and rebels sought safety at the abandoned Western Air Temple.

Once at the air temple, Jianjun began to sabotage various exits, seeking to hinder the movement of the Earth Kingdom rebels and refugees as well as give Uyanga's troops more time to arrive. Most importantly, she managed to destroy an elevator and tunnel which presented the easiest entryways into the structure through explosives. Yet her activities were noticed by a refugee, Woong, and an insurgent, Xinyan; to distract them, she blamed the explosions on the activities of a local spirit named Tien.
